The court heard Tiffani had Rett syndrome, a rare neurological disorder causing growth issues, and weighed just 13 kilograms; her teacher Nicola Reid said she did not appear to deteriorate during 2021 and had a healthy appetite, though the diagnosis could not be confirmed. Justice Pink noted there was evidence that Tiffani had not received medical care for a prolonged period before her death. Ms Scholten's sister Cassandra Dunn told the court that Richardson's relationship with Carrissa Scholten was controlling and abusive, describing him as short-tempered and possessive, and said he had snapped in multiple phone calls and voicemails despite only one physical altercation between them. Dunn alleged Richardson was a cocaine dealer who kept drugs hidden behind a fake power point in the bedroom, that his drug associates were raided by police shortly before Tiffani's death on April 18, 2022, and that Carrissa Scholten had been too afraid to seek medical help for her daughter over fears it would expose Richardson. Dunn said Carrissa was scared of how Richardson would react if she took Tiffani to the hospital. Teacher aide Brenda Walker testified that Tiffani last attended school in December 2021 and missed 16 weeks during 2022, while Carrissa Scholten attempted to feed her on the night before her death. Both defendants declined to speak in court and were not required to enter a plea; their trial date has yet to be determined.
items.title: Mother and stepfather stand trial over alleged murder of 12-year-old girl

items.summary: Police revealed that a fourth Melbourne Cup, this time a replica, had been stolen during a series of break-ins at Melbourne racecourses over the Spring Racing Carnival. The thefts are alleged to be linked: thieves dressed as tradies took Makybe Diva's three consecutive Melbourne Cups, won in 2003, 2004 and 2005 and worth $3 million, from Flemington Racecourse on Monday, while the 1948 Caulfield Cup was allegedly swiped from Caulfield Racecourse during several break-ins between November 4 and November 11. It had initially been believed that only Makybe Diva's three cups were taken from Flemington, but police allege a cup was stolen four days earlier. The Victoria Racing Club has remained tight-lipped about whether it knew of the first robbery before Makybe Diva's cups were taken. Two men have now been charged over the heists: Sama Mirzaagha and Chrysovalandis Tassakos, both expected to face court again in February. At a hearing in Melbourne Magistrates' Court on Monday, Mr Mirzaagha was out on bail at the time and not present; his lawyers described the prosecution as rushed and called the brief flimsy with serious deficiencies, while prosecutor Jonathon McCarthy said the evidence included DNA, fingerprints and extensive CCTV footage. Further details of the alleged offending were not read out in court, and Magistrate Simon Zebrowski refused to publicly release a remand summary filed by police. Mr Mirzaagha's charges include burglary, theft and dealing with property suspected of being proceeds of crime; he is normally prescribed medication and requested to be seen by a nurse in custody, though his lawyers did not apply for bail at that time but said an application would follow. His co-accused, Mr Tassakos, was granted bail earlier on charges including burglary, theft, handling stolen goods, dealing with property suspected of proceeds of crime, obtaining financial advantage and obtaining property by deception; he is charged in relation to both alleged heists and was supported in court by his parents. Police had raided a Mount Waverley home as part of their hunt for the cups, which remain missing.
items.title: Fourth Melbourne Cup Stolen as Two Men Charged Over Linked Heists

items.summary: The Euronews program Europe Today reports that Chinese President Xi Jinping, Russian President Vladimir Putin, and US President Donald Trump are set to meet for a historic trilateral summit at the APEC summit in Shenzhen. According to Kremlin critic Bill Browder and Euronews' Russian edition editor Serguei Doubine, who provide analysis of the meeting's consequences, the three leaders are expected to discuss denuclearization and the Iran war, but not Ukraine. Following this summit, Trump's envoys Jared Kushner and Steve Witkoff will travel to Berlin for a meeting of the 'Coalition of the Willing,' which is set to convene with senior officials from Ukraine along with its top European allies as well as NATO and EU representatives. The program obtains updates on these developments through Ignacy Niemczycki, Poland's Deputy Foreign Minister. Europe Today airs every weekday at 8 am, 9 am, and 10 am Brussels time across Euronews' TV channel, website, and digital platforms including YouTube, Facebook, X, and Instagram, presented by Stefan Grobe in a new format that runs for just 28 minutes covering the day's key events plus analysis of stories shaping the EU and beyond. The program is also available as a newsletter.
items.title: Europe Today: Xi, Trump and Putin trilateral meeting in Shenzhen

items.summary: On Thursday, 19 November 2026, while attending the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) summit in Shenzhen, China, President Donald Trump told Fox News that both the United States and China conduct espionage against one another. He stated, "We spy on China, they spy on us," and added his assessment that Washington is more effective at intelligence gathering than Beijing, saying, "I think we spy better than they do." When asked whether he would ask China to stop spying on the US, Trump suggested such a request was unlikely to succeed given America's own intelligence activities. He remarked, "They'll ask me to stop doing it, and I don't know if I'd do that." The remarks followed his planned unprecedented trilateral meeting with Chinese President Xi Jinping and Russian President Vladimir Putin at the summit. Trump also stressed the importance of maintaining relations with Beijing, citing extensive bilateral economic ties between the two countries.
items.title: Trump Says US and China Spy on Each Other, Claims Washington Is More Effective

items.summary: Around 100 corporations and industry groups tied to fossil fuels, including ExxonMobil and TotalEnergies, have sent delegations to this year's global climate summit, COP31 in Turkey. This follows a pattern of heavy lobbyist presence at previous summits: more than 1,600 attended the talks in Brazil last year, and more than 1,700 at the 2024 talks in Azerbaijan. The article argues that lobbyists slow the energy transition using what academics call "discourses of delay," spreading disinformation such as claims that fossil fuels are part of the solution or that future technologies will save us. Oil and gas companies reportedly increased their Google ads in the month before COP31, while researchers say lobbyists use a two-pronged strategy: pointing to lack of international action as an excuse for domestic inaction, and working to block progress at the talks themselves. A new UN report says it is now too late to hold global temperature rise to 1.5°C, with the world likely passing that threshold in 2030, partly due to lobbyist obstruction of policies targeting fossil fuels. At COP30, host country Brazil pushed back by launching an international partnership against climate disinformation alongside the UN and UNESCO; thirty countries have since signed onto a declaration condemning denialism and tactics undermining information integrity on climate change. Lobbyists gain access through affiliations with non-governmental organisations and industry groups as well as official government delegations, though this year's draft negotiating text references information integrity without establishing a clear code of conduct or meaningful disclosure of fossil fuel ties. Fossil fuels were only explicitly addressed at the Glasgow COP in 2021 after more than a quarter century of talks focused on greenhouse gas emissions rather than their source. Petrostates such as Russia and Saudi Arabia have assisted corporate lobbyists, while Azerbaijan and the United Arab Emirates used their hosting roles to push new fossil fuel deals. At COP31, negotiators are discussing more than 100 agenda items opposed by lobbyists, including a UN initiative to rapidly increase efforts to cut greenhouse gas emissions. In addition to the official agenda, COP President and Turkish Environment Minister Murat Kurum released a separate "action" agenda organised around ten themes, some of which threaten fossil fuel interests such as transitioning to clean energy. Lobbyists are likely targeting calls to phase out coal, gas and oil, echoing last year's failed efforts by Brazil to formalise a transition roadmap, along with an electrification goal aiming to boost electricity's share of final energy demand to 35% by 2035, which could reduce demand for oil and gas. Australia is on the tightrope as Climate Change Minister Chris Bowen acts as negotiation president under a co-hosting arrangement with Turkey; domestically, the Albanese Labor government has accelerated its energy transition through battery subsidies installed in more than 600,000 households since last year and rapidly growing electric vehicle uptake, while internationally Australia remains one of the world's largest coal and gas exporters. Prime Minister Anthony Albanese faced criticism for omitting fossil fuels from his opening speech, minutes after UN Secretary-General António Guterres urged countries to make fossil fuels "go the way of the dinosaurs." As COP31 enters its final days with eyes on Australia and Turkey, progress depends on whether co-hosts secure agreement advancing Brazil's transition efforts; meanwhile momentum for moving away from oil, gas and coal is gathering outside UN talks through an April international conference and a growing Fossil Fuel Non-Proliferation Treaty Initiative. The article concludes that clamping down on lobbyists and climate misinformation remains well overdue.
items.title: Fossil fuel lobbyists target COP31 as Australia co-hosts talks

items.summary: Spanish government figures report that more than 11,000 migrants reached the Canary Islands in the first 15 days of November alone, a record number for any single period. This figure represents more than half of the entire tally recorded across all of 2025. The surge is intensifying pressure on reception facilities and emergency services as authorities struggle to manage the volume of arrivals. Regional authorities have repeatedly warned about insufficient capacity, with some smaller islands facing populations equalled or exceeded by migrant numbers. In response, Spain declared a migration emergency in the Canary Islands on 10 November and allocated additional funds to expand capacity at state-run reception centres. A Red Cross spokesperson noted that most arrivals are from Senegal, Gambia, Mali, and Guinea, fleeing poverty and conflict in search of better lives in Europe. The islands remain a major entry point for migrants crossing the Atlantic Ocean in makeshift boats, predominantly from West and North Africa. The sharp rise in arrivals has become a prominent political issue ahead of Spain's 29 November general elections, with conservative politicians heavily criticising Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez over his government's immigration-friendly policies.
items.title: Record migrant arrivals strain Spain's Canary Islands

items.summary: Lyon marked its annual Beaujolais Nouveau release with a torchlit wine parade, as costumed revellers led wooden casks rolled down the city's streets or transported on tractors while trumpets blared. The festivities reached their peak at a staged theatrical uncorking of the season's first bottles, which triggered music, dancing and cheers as inaugural glasses were distributed to dense crowds. Beaujolais Nouveau originates from vineyards in the hills just north of Lyon and reaches shelves only weeks after harvest, sustaining what is described as a quintessential French autumn ritual. The wine is celebrated worldwide on the third Thursday of November, when it becomes legal at an exact stroke for producers to sell the new vintage; it is characterized as light and fruit-forward, intended for immediate enjoyment rather than long ageing. What began as a local harvest marker has evolved into a broad tribute to French winemaking heritage that brings producers and townspeople together in what organizers describe as an exuberant street festival.
items.title: Beaujolais Nouveau Release Celebrated in Lyon

items.summary: US President Donald Trump touted an "outstanding personal relationship" with Chinese President Xi Jinping during bilateral talks held Thursday, 19 November 2026, in the Chinese city of Shenzhen on the sidelines of the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) forum. Describing relations that began with his first state visit to China in 2017 and have grown "closer and closer" over nine years, Trump said he and Xi sat together for two hours during Wednesday evening's APEC welcome banquet and cultural performance to discuss key issues ahead of their formal session, adding that "I think something will come out." The leaders were expected to address trade issues, tariffs, and technology restrictions, including on chips. Reviewing economic ties, Trump pointed to the US-China Board of Trade established during his May visit to Beijing and the "30 for 30" tariff-relief proposal finalized during Xi's September state visit to Washington, under which each side agreed to cut tariffs on $30 billion of imports in a "very fair way." He said he would ask Beijing to expand agricultural purchases to meet China's "insatiable appetite." The meeting marked Trump's second visit to China this year and the third round of talks between the two leaders. In their last two summits, they agreed to "build a constructive relationship of strategic stability based on respect, fairness and reciprocity." Speaking for both leaders, Trump said Washington and Beijing want to help end the Russia-Ukraine war, noting that 25,000 people, "mostly soldiers" per month are being killed. Addressing the Iran situation, he said both nations share a strong interest in ensuring energy flows through the Strait of Hormuz and preventing Tehran from acquiring a nuclear weapon, stating "We both feel that very strongly on both points." Trump also highlighted counternarcotics as one area of potential cooperation, claiming seaborne fentanyl flows have fallen 97% following strict enforcement. The bilateral meeting followed Trump's talks with Russian President Vladimir Putin, and the three leaders were expected to hold trilateral discussions later Thursday; confirming that his earlier encounter with Putin served "just to set the stage," Trump predicted "maybe a successful" trilateral meeting. Earlier Thursday, Xi hosted the 33rd summit of APEC forum leaders. Fox News initially reported that the meeting lasted 13 minutes before removing its post, with subsequent reporting indicating talks ended at 2.35 pm local time (0635 GMT), lasting around one hour.
items.title: Trump and Xi Hold Bilateral Talks in Shenzhen Amid APEC Forum

items.summary: Sotheby's sold Vincent van Gogh's Châtaigniers en fleurs, known as Chestnut Trees in Blossom, at auction in New York on Wednesday for a record $190.4 million (£144.8 million). The price shattered the artist's previous auction high of $117.2 million set in 2022 and exceeded its pre-sale estimate of $180 million (£136 million). Painted in 1890 during the final two months of Van Gogh's life, Sotheby's describes it as one of the most important works from that period to remain in private hands. The sale came after an eleventh-hour agreement resolved a dispute over the painting's Nazi-era history. Representatives for the heirs of the Fischer family had claimed the work may have been sold under duress during the rise of the Nazis, writing to Sotheby's on their behalf and asserting it was sold in Amsterdam before World War Two because of financial losses suffered by the Fischer publishing company under the Nazis. In recognition of the painting's complex Nazi-era history and the suffering endured by the Fischer family during the Holocaust, the Blaquier-Arrieta family and the heirs reached a mutually satisfactory resolution, with Sotheby's stating the work would be sold pursuant to their agreement. The buyer was not immediately identified, though the BBC had contacted Sotheby's for comment. The painting was offered as part of the Blaquier-Arrieta Collection. Its provenance traces back through several owners: Samuel Fischer acquired it in 1909 before his death in 1934; it passed to Henriette and Marcel Kapferer in Paris in 1936 after being deposited with Paul Cassirer in Amsterdam in 1932 or 1933, followed by four further owners. The Blaquier family acquired the work in 1975 and held it for more than half a century before its sale.
items.title: Van Gogh painting sells for record $190.4m after Nazi-era provenance dispute resolved

items.summary: Indian auto stocks surged on Wednesday, led by Maruti Suzuki, India's largest carmaker, which jumped over 6.5% to Rs 13,487 per share on the BSE and topped the pack of gainers. Tata Motors Passenger Vehicles rose 4%, Mahindra & Mahindra (M&M) advanced 5% to Rs 3,508 per share, Hyundai Motor India shares climbed over 4% to Rs 2,193 apiece, and commercial vehicle maker Ashok Leyland gained over 2%. The Nifty Auto index jumped 4%, with the rally attributed to falling metal prices. On Wednesday, benchmark three-month copper on the London Metal Exchange (LME) fell for a fifth consecutive session, reaching its lowest level since April 13 before recovering marginally Thursday. Tim Waterer, chief market analyst at KCM Trade, told Reuters that the move in LME copper looked more like relief than a decisive turn, driven by a buoyant US dollar and growing uncertainty over the pace of AI data-center buildout, where copper is a key input. China's uneven economic recovery and concerns about demand from its construction and manufacturing sectors also weighed on sentiment, while higher crude oil prices added pressure across the mining, smelting, refining, and transportation chain. Aluminium and zinc are particularly sensitive to power costs. Analysts note that rising energy costs can curb business activity, industrial production, and consumer spending, ultimately weakening demand for metals used in construction, machinery, infrastructure, and automobiles. The decline in copper, aluminium, and tin prices could provide relief to Indian automakers by lowering raw-material costs, since these metals are used in vehicle manufacturing, electrical components, wiring, engines, and other auto parts; aluminium, copper, rubber, and plastic components account for 40-45% of passenger vehicle raw material costs. Foreign brokerage Jefferies said the earnings outlook for auto OEMs weakened in CY26 primarily due to the intense commodity cost rally, while the industry faces a high base of volumes starting 2HFY27 as commodity cost pressures continue at a lower intensity than seen in the first half of the financial year.
items.title: Indian Auto Stocks Rally as Metal Prices Fall

items.summary: Sarvam has begun selling access to Chinese AI models, including DeepSeek, Moonshot AI and Z.AI Co., through its new Token Factory inference platform. The service offers multiple open-weight systems via a single API interface hosted on local computing infrastructure in Bangalore. Sarvam is valued at $1.5 billion as of April and serves as the poster child for India's push to build AI services tailored to Indian languages and cultures, with Prime Minister Narendra Modi's government arguing that countries beyond the US and China must control their own destiny in emerging technology. The controversy stems from Sarvam's history: it built its frontier model on backing from the government's IndiaAI Mission and was one of the first local startups given subsidized compute. Co-founder Pratyush Kumar defended the company, saying "We haven't changed our motto" and that they continue to build AI models for India as a full stack AI company. He explained that selling tokens generates revenue needed to sustain the capital-intensive business of building models. The startup already serves over 450 billion tokens daily on DeepSeek V4.1 Flash, per its blogpost. Co-founder Vivek Raghavan emphasized that the infrastructure hosting the new service is separate and runs on computational power financed by investors, noting "Those chips are entirely funded by private money." He argued that using models hosted on outside servers risks data exfiltration, so Sarvam's offering keeps India's AI users' data within its borders. Otherwise, he said, Indians would pay for tokens and then double-pay with the data their own information amasses.
items.title: Sarvam sells DeepSeek access amid India AI independence backlash

items.summary: In an interview with ET AI at the Bengaluru Tech Summit, Kris Gopalakrishnan, former CEO and co-founder of Infosys and chairman of Axilor Ventures, argued that India must build its own artificial intelligence capability rather than depend on a single technology provider. He cited two warning signs: the US decision earlier this year to block access to some frontier AI models, and Microsoft outages that disrupted companies worldwide. Gopalakrishnan urged diversification, telling ET AI not to put all eggs in one basket and advising companies like Microsoft against relying on a single solution, adding that if an organization does not provide its own plan B, customers will choose it for them. He linked these concerns to technology sovereignty and strategic autonomy, insisting India must become self-sufficient. On the question of whether India should focus on frontier models or the application layer, Gopalakrishnan supported both, arguing the country needs the ability to develop its own models alongside businesses that apply AI. He noted significant Indian needs in healthcare, education, logistics, and manufacturing that AI could address, stating the app economy is five to eight times bigger than the model economy or data centre economy. For him, this opportunity includes bringing quality healthcare and education to underserved populations and improving productivity across industries, with AI expected to become part of products throughout the economy, including cars. On chips, costs, and adoption, Gopalakrishnan said India's ambitions should extend across the entire AI stack, including semiconductors, processors, and GPU manufacturing, while also producing new AI-based products. He identified next-generation processors as an opportunity, particularly those that use less power and cost less, because affordability would shape how India could deploy the technology. For businesses, he said realizing value from AI requires changes to people, systems, and processes: enterprises must understand a technology's benefits and drawbacks, retrain employees, integrate AI with existing systems, rethink business processes, and consider what happens to workers when technology eliminates categories of work. Asked what would show India got AI right five years out, he pointed to continued IT services growth and new AI products and capabilities across the stack, while acknowledging some efforts will take longer than others.
items.title: Kris Gopalakrishnan on AI, Microsoft outages

items.summary: Benchmark Indian equity indices fell on Thursday morning, extending losses from Wednesday as hawkish language in the minutes of a United States Federal Reserve meeting and a stronger dollar dampened global risk appetite. The Nifty 50 opened at 25,186.80 against a previous close of 25,227.95 and traded at 25,149.85, down 78.10 points or 0.31 per cent as of 9.27 am; the Sensex opened at 82,074.16 against a previous close of 82,031.81 and fell to 81,802.00, shedding 229.81 points or 0.28 per cent. Wednesday had already seen the Nifty shed 159.45 points, or 0.63 per cent, closing at 25,227.95, while the broader market weakened with the Nifty Midcap 100 falling 1.22 per cent and the Nifty Smallcap 100 declining 0.35 per cent, as the BSE advance-decline ratio slumped to 0.52 reflecting broad-based selling pressure. Information technology stocks were the sharpest drag on Thursday morning: Infosys fell 2.49 per cent to Rs 1,081.20 from a previous close of Rs 1,108.80, Tech Mahindra declined 1.71 per cent to Rs 1,720.00 from Rs 1,750.00, and HCL Technologies lost 1.70 per cent to Rs 1,321.80 from Rs 1,344.70. The rupee's continued appreciation to 93.44 against the dollar, a seven-month high, has added pressure on export-sensitive IT earnings.
items.title: Indian benchmark indices slip on hawkish Fed signals and IT weakness

items.summary: A report by The Information has drawn senior Indian-American Nvidia executive Jay Puri into the widening scandal surrounding the company's business ties to China. According to short-selling firm Muddy Waters, 71-year-old Puri joined Nvidia in 2005 and ran its global sales operation for nearly two decades, effectively serving as third-in-command after Jensen Huang and acting CEO Colette Kress before stepping down at the end of June while remaining a senior adviser. The report states that Puri oversaw chip sales to Alice Huang, who has been central to the scandal after US intelligence agencies reportedly believed she was a Chinese intelligence asset following revelations about her extramarital relationship with Jensen Huang, which forced him to resign as CEO last week. Separately, accounts of tensions at Nvidia's top emerged earlier this year during a prep call ahead of an AI summit in New Delhi, where Jensen Huang's daughter Madison reportedly called Puri out over poor planning after he pulled out of the event; people familiar with the matter said Puri interrupted to tell her she could have his answers if she stopped shouting. In another reported incident, Jensen Huang allegedly berated Puri in a closed-door meeting and told him he hoped he would die. Before Nvidia, Puri spent 22 years at Sun Microsystems in a leadership role within its Asia-Pacific business, holding engineering degrees from the University of Minnesota and Caltech plus an MBA from Harvard. The Daily Telegraph reported that Puri is married to Cenly Chen, a technology executive who worked for Super Micro Computer Inc (SMCI), whose employees were reportedly involved in illegally selling $2.5 billion worth of data servers with Nvidia graphics processing units to customers in China through a Singaporean front company. In March, the US government brought charges against three people linked to Chen's former company SMCI over these illegal sales; although Chen was not directly named as a defendant in a class action suit filed against SMCI, plaintiffs alleged that as a senior executive she likely knew of the illicit activities. Chen faces no criminal charges and Super Micro has denied that she controlled its Nvidia relationship. Puri gave no immediate response to the reports. Jensen Huang is expected to testify before lawmakers in Washington regarding semiconductor export controls and his relationship with Alice Huang.
items.title: Nvidia executive Jay Puri linked to chip sales involving Alice Huang

items.summary: Uday Kotak, founder and director of Kotak Mahindra Bank, raised the question of whether India Inc is undervalued while highlighting a sharp contrast between global AI company valuations and those of India's largest firms. In an X post, he pointed to Anthropic, the US-based developer behind the Claude chatbot, whose valuation has reached $1.5 trillion despite having existed for only about five years since its 2021 founding. Kotak noted that this figure exceeds the combined market capitalisation of India's top 10 companies and asked whether Indian firms are undervalued or need to catch up in the changing global business landscape, posing both possibilities: "Are we undervalued, or do we need to catch up in the new world? Or both?" Anthropic is preparing a public listing through an offering of 980 million shares, comprising 956.35 million newly sold shares and 23.65 million offered by existing shareholders. The IPO is expected to close on November 20, subject to customary conditions, with the issue price placing Anthropic's valuation above its previously targeted $1.4 trillion level; its final market capitalisation will depend on the total number of shares outstanding.
items.title: Anthropic IPO valuation surpasses India's top 10 companies combined; Kotak questions Indian valuations

items.summary:
Anthropic priced its initial public offering Wednesday in Oakland, California, setting a share price of USD 83 and valuing the artificial intelligence company at USD 1.5 trillion, according to AP reporting dated November 19. The deal raised USD 81 billion through 980 million shares—roughly 956 million sold by Anthropic itself and about 23.6 million offered by selling stockholders—and put the debut ahead of SpaceX's June offering, which raised approximately $75 billion. The pricing came above the company's initial range of USD 70 to USD 78 per share, signaling broad investor enthusiasm for AI stocks even amid market uncertainty tied to Nvidia's leadership turmoil and concerns about an AI bubble.

The San Francisco-based maker of the Claude tool is scheduled to begin trading on Thursday under the ticker symbol ANT on Nasdaq. Analyst Dan Ives described the pricing as evidence of strong demand among investors, calling it a big win for the tech sector after a turbulent period involving Nvidia's former CEO Jensen Huang and his personal controversies.

The company carries significant financial strain: USD 6.2 billion in debt that filings describe as substantial, unprofitability under standard accounting rules, and large spending commitments including leases requiring USD 900 billion on computing power over coming years, with USD 70 billion due within the next 12 months. The IPO offers a way to raise capital without adding further debt.

Anthropic competes directly with OpenAI—also formed in 2021 and not planning an IPO until next year—as well as Google, US startups, Chinese firms, and SpaceX's AI division. All three major players have lost more money than they earned due to the high costs of building AI systems.

CEO Dario Amodei cautioned in September that the industry should slow its pace so safety measures can keep up, warning otherwise about a swarm of agents potentially taking over the internet within months. Regulatory uncertainty looms as newly elected Democrats vow crackdowns amid backlash against data centers, with Texas and Georgia electing Democratic governors who pledged to halt new construction.

The company is structured as a public-benefit corporation that balances shareholder interests with long-term benefits for humanity. A long-term benefit trust can elect or remove a majority of the board but will not run day-to-day operations, potentially enabling strategies that may not maximize investor returns. Analyst Rich Lesser characterized AI market valuations as volatile over coming years—"up and down...but more up than down."
items.title: Anthropic's Record AI IPO at $1.5 Trillion Valuation

items.summary: Anthropic made its US stock market debut at a valuation of $1.5 trillion, with shares priced at $83 each on the Nasdaq Global Select Market under the symbol ANT. The offering comprised 980 million Class A common shares, of which Anthropic sold 956,351,354 and selling stockholders sold 23,648,646; trading was expected to begin November 19, 2026 with the deal closing on November 20, 2026. Underwriters received a 30-day option to buy up to an additional 147 million shares, and Anthropic stated it would receive no proceeds from the selling stockholders' portion of the sale. Founder and Director of Kotak Mahindra Bank, Uday Kotak, reacted to the listing by noting that its valuation surpasses the combined market capitalization of India's top 10 companies. He questioned whether Indian firms are undervalued or need to accelerate in new technologies such as AI, semiconductors, and data centers to compete in a rapidly shifting global economy, asking whether it is one problem or both. Kotak observed that Anthropic did not exist until about five years ago yet listed at $1.5 trillion. Financially, the company reported revenue of $33.2 billion for the first nine months of 2026, up over 1,200 percent year-over-year on demand for frontier AI models and infrastructure, while disclosing a net loss of $80 billion for the first half of 2026 despite rising revenue.
items.title: Kotak questions whether Indian companies are undervalued after Anthropic's $1.5 trillion IPO

items.summary:
Anthropic priced its initial public offering at USD 83 per share, topping the company's original range of USD 70 to USD 78 and valuing it at USD 1.5 trillion in what is being called the biggest Wall Street debut ever. The offering consists of 980 million shares, with roughly 956 million sold by Anthropic itself and about 23.6 million by selling stockholders. Proceeds totalling USD 81 billion put this IPO ahead of SpaceX's June raise of about $75 billion. Trading is set to begin Thursday on the Nasdaq under the ticker symbol "ANT".

The pricing above expectations signals broad investor enthusiasm for AI stocks even amid market uncertainty stemming from Jensen Huang's ouster as Nvidia CEO and worries about an AI bubble. Analyst Dan Ives called it a strong appetite for Anthropic, noting that the pricing shows strong demand among investors after a difficult period with Nvidia. The company had initially planned to offer 825 million shares but expanded its offering.

Anthropic proceeded despite investor jitters over market volatility, potential regulatory action by a Democratic-led Congress next year, and growing public anti-AI sentiment. The IPO lets employees sell vested stock for potentially large payouts while giving the company resources to accelerate expansion and benefiting CEO Dario Amodei and co-founder Daniela Amodei.

The company has taken on $6.2 billion in debt it acknowledges is "substantial," remains unprofitable under standard accounting rules, and faces limited ability to pay interest and principal despite ample cash for now. Anthropic signed leases requiring USD 900 billion in computing power spending over coming years, including USD 70 billion within the next 12 months.

An IPO provides capital instead of additional debt as borrowing costs rise due to inflation fears and the sector's massive financing needs, which have drawn comparisons to Gilded Age railroad expansion. Lenders worry AI companies carry too much debt without a clear path to profitability. Anthropic competes with OpenAI, Google, US startups, Chinese firms, and SpaceX.

Dario Amodei cautioned in September that the industry should slow development so safety measures can catch up, warning otherwise of AI agents potentially taking over the internet within months. The regulatory environment could shift once a new Congress convenes, with elected Democrats vowing to crack down on data centres amid backlash against them; Texas and Georgia just elected Democratic governors pledging to stop new construction.

Investors worry demand for AI shares could drop or collapse as several tech companies recently pulled IPO plans. Anthropic is a public-benefit corporation like OpenAI that balances shareholder interests with the public good, using a long-term benefit trust able to elect or remove a majority of its board while not running day-to-day operations.

Rich Lesser, former Boston Consulting Group CEO and global chair, said AI market valuation will be "up and down for many years to come, but more up than down," though the flow is hard to predict. He called what Anthropic, OpenAI, Google, and other players have done remarkable.
items.title: Anthropic's $1.5 Trillion IPO

items.summary: A storm over the Bay Area disrupted Microsoft Ignite on Wednesday, forcing a temporary closure of the conference's expo floor at San Francisco's Moscone Center. Rainwater leaked into the venue and soaked parts of the exhibition area, prompting KRON4 to confirm that portions of the space were cleared of attendees after rainwater came in. A Microsoft spokesperson said the Hub, as the expo floor is called, was shut temporarily because of weather-related issues. The disruption remained limited to the exhibition area; Microsoft stated that everything else at Ignite stayed open, including its innovation sessions and community events. The San Francisco City Administrator's Office told KRON4 that the exhibit hall closed due to the leak while the rest of Moscone Center remained open and the conference continued. Footage shared on X showed rain coming through the roof onto parts of the expo floor. The incident occurred as a major storm brought widespread power outages, road closures, and travel disruptions across the region, with the National Weather Service recording nearly 2 inches of rain in downtown San Francisco on Wednesday morning. Microsoft Vice President of Communications Doug Dawson said the expo floor would reopen Thursday with hours extended until 7:30 p.m., while sessions and community events continued as scheduled. Earlier that day, the company had promised to announce a reopening time once available. Ignite began Tuesday and runs through Friday at Moscone Center in San Francisco's South of Market district; it is Microsoft's flagship annual conference and returned to the city this year after criticism from some attendees about the venue and its layout.
items.title: Microsoft Ignite Expo Floor Closed After Storm Water Leak

Tao Lin, an Anthropic researcher who has worked at the company for roughly a year and a half, warned in an interview with Palisade Research that artificial intelligence could soon outperform humans across nearly every field. He made his remarks while working on safeguards involving monitoring requests to Claude and blocking harmful ones, including those about weapons and hacking; he previously focused on automated alignment research and AI control. Lin defined 'broadly superhuman' as systems matching or exceeding the best human expert in almost every domain, citing programming, filmmaking, and politics as examples. He gave his own forecast for reaching that point at around 1.3 years from now, roughly late 2027, while noting this is a personal prediction rather than an official Anthropic position.

On employment, Lin said the most predictable outcome would be nearly everyone losing their current job and shifting to another occupation. He then argued people could become permanently unemployable with no realistic chance of returning to work, relying instead on state financial support as human employment effectively disappears. He cautioned this would not occur overnight, since replacing physical labor at scale would first require companies to build better robots and manufacture billions of them.

Lin estimated the probability that AI would eventually remove humanity from the equation at around 20 percent, placing direct extinction as unlikely and an AI takeover below 50 percent. He described such a takeover as potentially leaving humans alive and content but without control over the world, comparing it to the animated film WALL-E.

Lin urged AI companies to cut their research pace to about one quarter of the current rate. He argued that competitive pressure to ship models quickly leaves too little time for safety testing, while slowing down would give researchers room to improve safety practices and keep systems under human control.
items.title: Anthropic researcher Tao Lin warns of permanent AI-driven unemployment

items.summary: The Deccan Herald quoted India's Commerce Secretary Rajesh Agrawal as saying on Wednesday that although negotiations for a bilateral trade agreement with the United States are close to finalisation, the deal will not be signed until Washington establishes a new tariffs framework. After an interim trade deal was agreed upon on February 2, US tariffs on Indian goods would have been reduced from a combined rate of 50% to 18%. The earlier 50% rate had included a punitive levy of 25% imposed in August 2025 over India's purchase of Russian oil. Negotiations on the final deal were hampered after the US Supreme Court struck down global tariffs imposed by President Donald Trump on February 20, ruling that he had exceeded his authority. In response, Trump imposed a temporary 10% tariff on goods imported into the US under the 1974 Trade Act, leaving the status of trade deals with all countries, including India, unclear. Agrawal was quoted as saying that all aspects of the deal were 'more or less finalised' and an interim agreement was imminent. However, he said the deal could only be signed after the US's new tariff framework comes into effect and investigations under Section 301 are concluded; the provision allows the US to investigate and impose tariffs or trade sanctions against countries over unfair trade practices. Agrawal stated that 'you can't have a deal till you have got uncertainty around multiple investigations,' adding that the numbers and actual deal would be signed once these investigations reach maturity. He made the comments at an event organised by the Federation of Indian Chambers of Commerce and Industry. Separately, Agrawal said the government was trying to conclude negotiations on other trade deals by the end of the year, with 'good news' expected in December; The Times of India reported this as a reference to ongoing talks with Canada, during which Prime Minister Narendra Modi is expected to visit.
items.title: India delays signing US trade deal pending new tariff framework

On Thursday, Prime Minister Narendra Modi paid tribute to former Prime Minister Indira Gandhi on her birth anniversary via a post on X, describing it as an occasion to remember her contributions to the country. Several Congress leaders joined in the tributes, including Lok Sabha opposition leader Rahul Gandhi, who honored his grandmother by sharing a conversation between his mother Sonia Gandhi and sister Priyanka about Indira Gandhi, calling her formidable, fearless, resilient, and full of love. Rahul added that she would be proud of them. Priyanka Gandhi Vadra described Indira Gandhi as a tigress and said there would never be another leader like her. Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge, Sonia Gandhi, and other senior leaders paid floral tributes at the central hall of Samvidhan Sadan in New Delhi. Karnataka chief minister D K Shivakumar marked the occasion by describing Indira Gandhi as the Iron Lady and highlighting her role in shaping India's political and economic landscape, pointing to contributions to agriculture, banking, and the country's space and nuclear programmes during her tenure.

The tributes came on the birth anniversary of Indira Gandhi, who was born on November 19, 1917, in Allahabad, now Prayagraj in Uttar Pradesh, as the daughter of India's first Prime Minister Jawaharlal Nehru. She became the country's first woman Prime Minister and held office from 1966 to 1977 before returning for a second term in 1980. Indira Gandhi served until her assassination in 1984, after which her son Rajiv Gandhi took over as Prime Minister.
items.title: Indian leaders pay tribute to Indira Gandhi on birth anniversary

items.summary: At a United Nations Security Council Arria-formula meeting convened by Liberia on natural resources and conflict, India's Permanent Representative to the UN, Ambassador Parvathaneni Harish, sharply criticized Pakistan after that delegation raised the Indus Waters Treaty. Harish said New Delhi had no intention of introducing bilateral issues into the discussion but was compelled to respond because he believed Pakistan chose to misuse the forum by peddling its propaganda; his position on the treaty remains clear and consistent and has been articulated at multiple fora, he added. He targeted Pakistan's military establishment, referring to an incident in which army chief Asim Munir displayed a wooden case containing mineral stones to foreign leaders last September as evidence of the army's role in resource exploitation. Harish linked this activity to political developments within Pakistan, including the dismissal of an elected provincial government and the imposition of a state of emergency there. He noted that last year PM Shehbaz Sharif and Munir were photographed presenting rare earth minerals to US President Donald Trump at the White House, with Munir gesturing toward an open wooden case containing the minerals while Trump looked inside and Sharif stood nearby. Harish warned that Pakistan's military prioritizes its own interests over ordinary citizens and accused it of fomenting conflict among neighbouring countries in a way that is boomerang-ing back to bite their own country, arguing that Pakistani leaders would be served better if they used the nation's natural resources for public benefit rather than self-aggrandisement. Beyond this exchange with Pakistan, Harish outlined India's view on responsible resource management, contending that illegal mining and smuggling can finance armed groups and prolong conflicts instead of advancing national development; he praised Liberia for convening the discussion because its own journey from conflict to recovery lends weight to the topic. He called for greater reliance on existing voluntary international mechanisms rather than new frameworks, citing the Kimberley Process as an example of effective cooperation between governments, industry and civil society that has curbed trade in conflict diamonds while keeping legitimate trade open; India is chairing the process in 2026 and remains committed to strengthening its effectiveness and inclusiveness. Harish emphasized that existing and tested mechanisms deserve full use before new frameworks are contemplated, stressed that local communities should benefit from resources extracted from their land under India's mining laws requiring companies to contribute toward development of affected areas, and argued for respecting the distinct mandates of UN bodies so that the Security Council focuses on international peace and security while sustainable development and resource governance fall to the General Assembly, ECOSOC and other relevant institutions. The report is marked as untrusted source text.
items.title: India accuses Pakistan's military of exploiting its own natural resources

Kerala was the first Indian state to receive deep-sea fishing vessels under the Pradhan Mantri Matsya Sampada Yojana (PMMSY), a central government scheme launched in 2020 that aims to convert traditional daily fishers into deep-sea operators. In its first year, Kerala spent about ₹12 crores on manufacturing ten boats at an initial price of ₹1.2 crore each; the cost rose to ₹1.5 crore within three months. Beneficiaries were expected to contribute ₹72 lakhs per boat while central and state governments covered the rest. The state encouraged fisheries cooperatives to apply in groups of ten, helped them secure three-year loans from the Kerala Finance Corporation, selected six cooperative societies as beneficiaries, and sold six of the ten boats. The Central Institute of Fisheries Technology designed the vessels and Udupi Cochin Shipyard Ltd manufactured them.

Fishers were expected to spend at least 20 days at sea navigating choppy waters and returning with high-value species such as tuna, marlin, billfish and others for higher incomes. All six boat owners report similar problems: faulty cold storage that causes fish to rot, excessive fuel consumption, undersized machinery, water seepage into the engine room, and poorly designed steering controls dangerous in strong winds. Each beneficiary now faces debts of around ₹80 lakhs with mounting repair costs and no returns; none is currently using a boat received under the scheme.

The deep-sea fishing boats were expected to keep fishers at sea for at least 20 days, navigating choppy waters and returning with high-value species such as tuna, marlin, billfish and others. But all six boat owners report similar problems: faulty cold storage that causes fish to rot, excessive fuel consumption, undersized machinery, water seepage into the engine room, and poorly designed steering controls that make the boat dangerous to steer in strong winds.

Each beneficiary now faces debts of around ₹80 lakhs (₹8 million), with repair costs mounting and no returns on the investment. None of the beneficiaries is currently using the boat received under the scheme. Gillnetting and seine fishing boats go 70-80 km into the sea, spend 10-12 hours in the water and catch tuna, mackerel, sardines, and prawns. Hook-and-line boats can go 120 km into the sea and largely catch yellow-fin tuna.

However, over the last decade or so, fishers here have caught fewer fish. Harsh weather leads to fewer fishing days. Additionally, overfishing and the harvesting of juvenile fish, the impacts of climate change, as well as coastal construction that changes wave action and causes coastal erosion, have all affected fish availability.

The promise: Shaju Antony and Chacko (name changed) each invested ₹72 lakhs of their own money for a boat under the PMMSY and subsequently received the boats in 2023. The unravelling: These problems were compounded by how long the fishers were away from shore. Unlike daily fishing, where they return the same day and repair the boats if needed, deep-sea fishing expeditions can last up to a month. During such trips, boat troubles kept cropping up and hindered the work, and once out on a trip, they could not quit and come back halfway through.

Shaju Antony ended up paying an extra ₹30 lakhs (₹3 million) to repair the boat. In his letter he questioned whether it was assumed that because the boats were meant for fishermen, simply constructing and handing them over would suffice, asking why Udupi Cochin Shipyard acted irresponsibly.

Bringing home rotting fish and losses: Initially there was confusion about the fish-hold's function. Shaju Antony stated in his letter that descriptions said a freezer system meant no ice was needed; only when boats went fishing did it become clear the freezer merely kept carried ice from melting away, meaning fishers still need to carry ice for cooling.

But even with ice, fish continued to perish either because wooden partitions caused uneven cooling or because the compressor stopped functioning. The faulty cold storage room spoiled fish and increased operating costs since it ran on diesel; the generator consumes six litres of diesel an hour just to cool the room. If run continuously for 20 days, a deep-sea fishing trip uses about 2,880 litres worth ₹300,000, merely preventing ice worth ₹15,000 from melting.

Overall, a 20-day fishing trip uses 7,680 litres of diesel costing the fisher ₹8-10 lakhs (₹800,000 to ₹1 million), while caught fish fetch only ₹3-4 lakh (₹300,000-400,000) about half what is spent on diesel. In August 2025 the government announced revised guidelines addressing refrigeration inefficiencies that would help next lot of boats; by then it was too late for Kerala fishers who are now deep in debt.

Undersized machinery, steering issues and other problems: Siddharth Chakravarty, a fisheries research scholar, said two things were likely happening. The steering hydraulic pump is under-capacity so the rudder does not turn fast enough; second, the engine has low HP meaning enough wash across the rudder cannot be generated relative to beam width.

Ideally the hydraulic motor's power should match boat size: for a 75-feet long and 28-feet wide boat at least 10 HP is required. Antony said the provided 4 HP pump is not sufficient to move the boat with ease.

Disillusionment and debt: The vessel cost ₹1.5 crore; central and state governments together paid about half (around ₹74 lakh), while fishers invested the remaining half (around ₹72 lakh). This amount, raised through personal loans, pawning jewellery and using homes as collateral, also came from other villagers, cooperative members, and family who felt the scheme would be beneficial. Instead they are all left in various forms of debt; Peter and Shaju have both mortgaged their homes, while Joseph owes ₹60 lakhs (₹6 million) to his group.

Daily fishing returns as deep-sea dreams end: Protocols mandated that vessels primarily use domestically made parts under the Public Procurement (Preference to Make in India) Order 2017. Because of this Kerala fishers could not customise their boats, while fishers in Karnataka and Maharashtra have subsequently installed Chinese engines of at least 350 HP.

The amended SOPs for PMMSY deep-sea fishing vessels were released in August 2025, five years after the scheme launched. The amendment allowed FRP construction a lighter material than steel; it also made refrigeration optional so fishers would place ice and use that for cooling instead of running the compressor generator.

However Kerala fishers do not benefit from these guidelines. Mongabay-India reached out to officials at CIFT, Cochin Shipyard and the Kerala Fisheries department seeking comments but received no response.
items.title: Unfit PMMSY boats leave Kerala fishers in debt

items.summary: Reuters reported that Bangladesh deployed hundreds of paramilitary troops on Wednesday as talks of ousted Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina returning to the country triggered clashes, bomb blasts and arson attacks. The violence has been blamed on supporters of her banned Awami League party. On Saturday, Dhaka said it had completed the legal procedures required to secure Hasina's return from India, with the final decision on extraditing her resting with New Delhi. Hasina fled to India in August 2024 after having been in power for 16 years; her ouster came after several weeks of widespread student-led protests against her government. In November 2025 she was sentenced to death by Bangladesh's International Crimes Tribunal for crimes against humanity connected to a deadly crackdown on protesters in 2024. The former prime minister has reportedly requested a new passport and identity card from Dhaka, but the Bangladeshi government has so far rejected her request, prompting supporters of her party to take to the streets in protest. Last week the Awami League announced a week-long programme of demonstrations in support of Hasina's return, set to conclude with a nationwide strike on Thursday. Dozens of crude bomb blasts and torching of vehicles were recorded in at least 28 districts over the last 10 days; police data showed that at least 70 crude bomb explosions and 57 arson attacks on vehicles occurred between November 7 and November 17, per The Daily Star. Between November 1 and November 17, more than 520 persons were arrested for their alleged involvement in the unrest. On Tuesday a member of the ruling Bangladesh Nationalist Party was killed allegedly by unidentified persons during a protest near Hasina's home district of Gopalganj, on the day marking one year since her death sentence. At least 37 branches and offices of Grameen Bank were also targeted in arson attacks or attempted fires since November 10; Reuters quoted the firm as saying this. The bank was founded by Nobel laureate Muhammad Yunus, who led the country's interim government after Hasina's ouster until February and has faced alleged hostility from her supporters. Dhaka has repeatedly demanded that Hasina be extradited and expressed concerns about the ousted leader being allowed to address her supporters from Delhi; the Indian government said it was for Hasina to decide whether she wants to return to Bangladesh.
items.title: Bangladesh deploys paramilitary amid unrest over Hasina's return

Prachi Saroop, a senior Central Board of Indirect Taxes and Customs (CBIC) officer serving as Principal Chief Commissioner of the Mumbai CGST Zone, has submitted her resignation. She filed a formal three-month notice to Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman under Rule 43 of the CCS (Pension) Rules, 2012, citing personal reasons while thanking the government and her colleagues for their support. Saroop is among the senior-most officers in the department and had reportedly been viewed as a contender for a board seat.

According to The Secretariat, some staff members believe repeated setbacks in board selection may have influenced her decision. She was allegedly shortlisted and interviewed three times for a CBIC Member position but did not secure a seat on the board. Her request arrives ahead of another selection round for a CBIC Member that officials say is expected in the coming weeks.

Saroop holds a Master of Science degree and entered Group A service on September 16, 1991. She began as an Assistant Commissioner in the Chennai Central Excise Zone in May 1993 before handling central excise and customs assignments in Delhi. Her career progressed through Deputy Commissioner (2000) and Joint Commissioner (2002), including service at the Directorate General of Audit in Delhi and a deputation to the Department of Biotechnology as Deputy Secretary. Later postings covered service tax, central excise, customs, and vigilance work in Mumbai, where she served as Principal Commissioner in Mumbai Customs and Principal Additional Director General of Vigilance. She joined the Settlement Commission in Delhi in June 2023, became Chief Commissioner posted to Mumbai Customs Zone-III in August, and took charge as Principal Chief Commissioner of the Mumbai CGST Zone in April 2026.

Social media users reacted with speculation rather than factual statements. One user wrote that Saroop had been superseded by a junior for the Member post and claimed ego governs CBIC; another alleged she was taking time to enjoy her earnings before retirement; a third commented on how much she has earned. Officials countered that appointments follow a prescribed process and that seniority alone does not determine board membership.

The article is reported by Sounak Mukhopadhyay of LiveMint, whose bio describes his coverage across trending news, sports, entertainment, box office performance, digital culture, and cricket.
items.title: Senior IRS officer Prachi Saroop seeks voluntary retirement amid board selection speculation

items.summary: The Economic Times reports that LT Foods' share price rose 8% following its subsidiary's acquisition of US-based Maya Kaimal for $6 million. MK Food Holdings Inc., operating through its wholly owned subsidiary Maya Kaimal Foods LLC, markets premium Indian-inspired shelf-stable sauces, ready-to-eat curries and rice products under the Maya Kaimal brand, which it describes as a leading player among mainstream consumers in the premium Indian-inspired foods category. The company reported revenue of $17.9 million for the 12 months ended September 30, 2026, up from $15.5 million in the corresponding period of 2025. In its regulatory filing, LT Foods stated that the acquisition is an important strategic step to strengthen its Ready-to-Eat (RTE), Ready-to-Cook (RTC) and Ready-to-Heat (RTH) portfolio, noting that Maya Kaimal's culinary and product-development capabilities will complement LT Foods' existing strengths while enabling broader products, deeper engagement with US consumers, and new distribution and cross-category growth opportunities. Management emphasized that the United States remains a strategically important growth market for LT Foods, with plans to leverage combined business strengths to create scale, widen distribution, and unlock meaningful cross-category opportunities. Ashwini Arora, MD and CEO of LT Foods, said bringing together Maya Kaimal's consumer proposition and innovation capabilities with LT Foods' scale, market reach and execution strengths offers a strong platform for sustainable growth and long-term value creation in one of the company's most important global markets. The article is written by Veer Sharma, who is not a SEBI-registered Research Analyst or Investment Adviser and holds no financial interest in the companies mentioned as of publication.
items.title: LT Foods shares rise after Maya Kaimal acquisition

items.summary: The Supreme Court on Thursday listed a batch of petitions challenging India's marital rape exception for final hearing, fixing the matter for December 9 or 10 and aiming to hear it before the winter break that begins on December 21. The petitions raise whether a husband should be protected from prosecution when he forces his adult wife to have sex. This protection existed under Section 375 of the now-repealed Indian Penal Code and has been retained in Exception 2 to Section 63 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023, which states that sexual intercourse or acts by a man with his own wife is not rape if she is not under eighteen years of age. The petitions came before a bench of Chief Justice Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana. Senior advocate Indira Jaising requested the December listing because the court was scheduled to hear a partly heard case at 2 pm; the Chief Justice said, "We will either have it on December 2-3 or on December 9-10," noting that finishing the part-heard matter made same-day consideration impossible. On September 9, the Centre told the bench that its earlier response in the main case could also be treated as a reply to the other petitions, and the court said it would examine whether prosecution could continue if the exception remained in force and whether the exception was constitutionally valid. The Supreme Court first sought the Centre's response on January 16, 2023, regarding the IPC provision protecting husbands from prosecution for forced sexual intercourse with adult wives, and later issued notice to the Centre over a similar petition challenging the corresponding Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita provision. One of the petitions arose from the Delhi High Court's split verdict on May 11, 2022; Justices Rajiv Shakdher and C Hari Shankar agreed that substantial questions of law required Supreme Court intervention. Justice Shakdher favored striking down the marital rape exception as "unconstitutional," describing it as tragic if a married woman's call for justice went unheard after 162 years since the IPC was enacted, while Justice Shankar held the exception was not unconstitutional and rested on an intelligible difference. Separately, the Karnataka High Court had earlier ruled that exempting husbands from allegations of rape and unnatural sex with their wife contradicted Article 14's guarantee of equality before the law. The Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, along with the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita and the Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam, came into effect on July 1, 2024, replacing the Indian Penal Code, the Code of Criminal Procedure, and the Evidence Act.
items.title: Supreme Court to Hear Marital Rape Exception Petitions in December

items.summary: Defence stocks including HAL, Bharat Dynamics and others rose up to 3% after Defence Secretary Singh said at the FICCI Annual General Meeting curtain-raiser that India's defence capital expenditure budget for FY27 was set at Rs 2.19 lakh crore. The ministry is seeking a further 20% capex hike, with officials citing the outlay's multiplier effect on the economy alongside higher contracts and stronger demand signals to industry. Singh said the ministry aims to sign another record value of contracts and remains confident it can meet its export target of Rs 50,000 crores at least one year in advance. India's defence exports reach around 80 countries across equipment from artillery guns to bulletproof jackets, reflecting growing maturity of the domestic industry; Singh added that fairly significant platform exports are expected. Separately, Defence Minister Rajnath Singh said during a visit to Japan on Wednesday that India's defence sector is moving beyond self-reliance toward strengthening its global standing, with production and exports expanding at unprecedented speed as Army, Navy and Air Force capabilities grow alongside indigenous manufacturing. On the market side, defence stocks surged up to 50% in one month last year after military strikes against terrorist outfits under Operation Sindoor, before facing profit booking; strong capex plans supported them overall even during an earlier sharp selloff amid rising oil prices from a Middle East conflict. The Nifty India Defence index has gained 14.5% in 2026 so far and over 7% in one year, though it fell 3% in one week, 4% in one month and more than 11% in three months.
items.title: India defence stocks rise on record production and capex hike hopes

The Odisha Legislative Assembly was adjourned until 4 pm on Thursday after opposition parties disrupted proceedings. The Biju Janata Dal sought a debate on recent floods in Ganjam district, while the Congress raised the Kotia border dispute with Andhra Pradesh. Members of both parties displayed placards and shouted slogans during the disruption.

The disturbance began at Question Hour when the House assembled at 10.30 am. Opposition members entered the well of the House before Speaker Surama Padhy took her seat. When she allowed Parliamentary Affairs Minister Mukesh Mahaling to answer a question, opposition members raised slogans; some stood at the reporters' table while others shouted from below the Speaker's podium. Congress MLA Taraprasad Bahinipati was seen banging the podium during his anti-BJP protests.

The House conducted business for only seven minutes before the Speaker adjourned proceedings until 4 pm. BJD MLA Sarada Prasanna Jena told Press Trust of India that the party had submitted a motion to the Speaker a day before the session began, requesting a discussion on the flood issue after suspending all House business. He stated that when the Speaker did not act on their notice, there was no alternative but to demand a discussion themselves.
items.title: Odisha Assembly adjourned amid BJD and Congress disruptions over floods and border dispute

items.summary: The Indian Air Force showcased its air power and disaster-response capabilities on Thursday through a large-scale demonstration at Air Force Station Jamnagar as part of 'Sahayata Setu 2026', the annual joint Humanitarian Assistance and Disaster Relief exercise held from November 17 to 19. The drill involved coordinated operations by the Army, Navy and Air Force alongside the Indian Coast Guard, national disaster management agencies, civil administrations, and representatives from friendly foreign countries. Chief of Defence Staff General N S Raja Subramani emphasized that effective humanitarian response requires a whole-of-nation approach rather than action by any single agency, noting India's role as a dependable first responder in the Indian Ocean region and Indo-Pacific under its Neighbourhood First policy and MAHASAGAR vision. He cited Operation Dost in Turkiye and Operation Brahma in Myanmar as examples of past humanitarian assistance operations. The exercise focused on joint preparedness, clearly defined responsibilities, interoperability, and effective use of technology, with the goal of translating coordination into timely action. Participating aircraft included IAF Jaguar fighters, C-130J Super Hercules transport planes, Mi-17 helicopters, remotely piloted quadcopters for aerial reconnaissance, an Advanced Light Helicopter Mark IV operated by all three services, and the Indian Navy's Dornier aircraft alongside Army ALH and Cheetah helicopters. Demonstrations featured an Mi-17 V5 helicopter carrying a bucket to douse fires with firefighting robots support, another Mi-17 1B airlifting an Army vehicle, a Chinook heavy-lift helicopter transporting bridge components, and IAF Combat Free Fall Rapid Response Force personnel jumping from an AN-32 aircraft. The multinational AJHE-26 exercise aims to strengthen inter-agency synergy, operational interoperability, and international coordination in responding to cyclones, earthquakes, floods, and chemical emergencies.
items.title: IAF leads multi-agency HADR exercise in Gujarat

items.summary:
US President Donald Trump met Russian President Vladimir Putin on Thursday in Shenzhen, China, on the sidelines of the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) summit. The encounter was reported by Reuters as their first in-person meeting in more than a year. During the talks, Trump praised their long-standing relationship and friendship, telling Putin that he believed wonderful things could come out of it or at least start there.

The bilateral meeting set the stage for subsequent discussions with Chinese President Xi Jinping and a proposed trilateral summit involving all three leaders. According to Reuters' own quick-answers summary, this is described as a historic first trilateral meeting between the leaders of the US, China and Russia. Trump had earlier characterized the gathering as an opportunity to explore areas of cooperation among the major powers.

No official agenda has been announced for the proposed summit. Possible topics reportedly include nuclear arms control, the Iran war, global trade, and the Russia-Ukraine war. Additional subjects could cover supply-chain security, economic cooperation, artificial intelligence, digital infrastructure, and technology governance. White House spokeswoman Olivia Wales told reporters that Trump would discuss reducing nuclear weapons worldwide, which she said he considers very dangerous to proliferate.

On several sensitive issues, expectations remain uncertain. The US does not expect the meeting to produce an agreement, though Trump is expected to raise concerns about nuclear reduction and proliferation; China has been reluctant to join formal arms-control negotiations. White House officials indicated that Trump was not expected to raise the Russia-Ukraine war, although he suggested he might bring it up.

Separately speaking to Fox News, Trump said he would not seek help from Russia and China to end the Iran conflict. Earlier on Wednesday, Xi Jinping welcomed Trump at Shenzhen airport, marking the first time he had personally received a visiting leader there since becoming president; the two leaders shared a brief hug.

The summit also comes days after a controversy in which an alleged Chinese spy reportedly "honey trapped" former Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang, resulting in his departure from the company and tighter US controls on exporting advanced American semiconductors. The article's author is Prabhakar Jha, a digital news editor with nearly a decade of experience who joined LiveMint as a Digital Content Producer in 2026.
items.title: Trump, Putin and Xi to hold historic trilateral meeting in China

items.summary: A dispute arose over MPP elections in AP's Nellimarla constituency on Thursday, centered on the allocation of two posts: Bhogapuram and Pusapatirega. The TDP leadership is reportedly prepared to allot both these MPP posts to the Jana Sena. However, the decision to give the Pusapatirega post to the Jana Sena has drawn resentment among certain TDP leaders, because former minister Pativada Narayanaswamy's son is contesting for that same post. The affected TDP leaders have expressed disappointment over being denied an opportunity for their family member in this matter. Separately, in the Achanta gram panchayat elections, sarpanch candidate Kodidela Satyanarayana released an election manifesto containing 10 promises aimed at village development, including a pledge to spend 50 per cent of his personal earnings on such development if elected.

items.summary:
The Indian government has broadened financial and logistical assistance available to exporters through amendments to four interventions under the Niryat Disha sub-scheme of the ₹25,060-crore Export Promotion Mission (EPM), made on November 17. The changes target three persistent challenges facing exporters: limited access to overseas markets, rising costs of meeting international quality standards, and high logistics expenses. The amendments are especially significant for micro, small and medium enterprises (MSMEs) and first-time exporters that lack the financial resources and established networks available to larger firms, reflecting a shift toward extending support beyond traditional export clusters.

Under the Market Access Support (MAS) intervention, the maximum eligible export turnover threshold for airfare reimbursement was raised from ₹75 lakh to ₹50 crore. Micro and small exporters can now receive up to 95% of airfare costs for participating in international trade fairs, buyer-seller meets and trade delegations, while other eligible exporters may claim up to 80%. The mandatory membership period with Export Promotion Councils was also reduced from six months to three months. Officials note that the longer-term benefits will depend on whether participation translates into sustained buyer relationships and actual export orders.

The Trade Regulations, Accreditation and Compliance Enablement (TRACE) intervention expanded its coverage by increasing the number of certificates eligible for reimbursement from 462 to 600, addressing compliance costs associated with quality, safety, traceability and sustainability requirements in regulated markets. The largest geographical expansion came under the Logistics Interventions for Freight and Transport (LIFT) component, which extended low export-intensity district coverage from 13 to 34 states and Union Territories. LIFT also added Land Customs Stations and Integrated Check Posts among eligible port categories, incorporated waterways alongside existing road, rail and air transport modes, extended air freight assistance to Jammu and Kashmir and Ladakh, and reduced the minimum distance eligibility requirement between origin and destination ports from 200 km to 100 km. The intervention will cover all exportable merchandise except items on a negative list.

The Federation of Indian Export Organisations (FIEO) president S C Ralhan welcomed the changes as addressing exporters' three critical requirements: access to international markets, affordability of quality certifications, and high logistics costs. He described the raised airfare threshold and enhanced 95% assistance for micro and small exporters as major enabling measures that reduce financial burdens, while wider geographical coverage could encourage new export hubs.

The EPM was approved by the Union Cabinet in November 2025 with an outlay of ₹25,060 crore for FY26-FY31. It operates through two sub-schemes: Niryat Protsahan, focused on trade finance, and Niryat Disha, addressing market access and non-financial export barriers. The article notes that the amendments' effectiveness will ultimately depend on timely reimbursements, ease of application, and awareness among smaller exporters, with the broader test being whether lower entry costs create a more geographically diversified export base supporting India's ambition to strengthen its position in international trade.
items.title: India widens export support and raises airfare subsidy to 95% for small exporters
